why: I compared all seven verifier checks with their expect lines, and none asks for more than the line's words. Checks 1–5 use cmp to test only the exact stdout plus a newline, and check 1 also tests "exits 0". The expect lines say "prints exactly", so a byte-exact comparison is what they require. Check 5 builds the expected text with printf '\\t', which gives a literal backslash-t and matches the line. Check 6 passes on npm test exit=0 plus one test that runs bin/csv2json.js with --tsv on input containing tabs and "asserts on what it outputs". That is exactly what the line says. Check 7 needs only a mention of --tsv and an example command that uses it. The stricter parts sit under "Advisory (not part of PASS/FAIL)": the npm run test:cli mismatch, the README saying the flag means tab-separated input, and the flag-position test. No PASS or FAIL condition adds a mutation test, scope rule or exact-wording rule.
